messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private fastpatch readiness & escape plan for AcmeHealth VPC

Team / Acme ops,

We have a zero-day kernel mitigation that needs to be applied to AcmeHealth's private deployment (VPC) packages next week. This is a micro-patch (no schema changes) but touches the inference runtime and requires a short process: pinning the control plane agent, draining KV caches, applying patch, smoke-run, and then unpin.

Goals for this thread:
- Confirm maintenance window options (primary ask: minimize cross-day user impact)
- Finalize canary cohort and rollback triggers
- Confirm automation pieces (drain script, pin mechanism, post-checks)

Proposed maintenance windows (pick one):
- Option A: Wed 2028-07-03 01:00-03:00 PT (low US usage)
- Option B: Sat 2028-07-06 02:00-05:00 PT (longer, ops-friendly)

Suggested canary: 5% of fleet in us-west (no stateful workloads), followed by 20% ramp after 15m of green metrics. Rollback trigger: any tail latency P95 increase > 40% or error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m.

I've attached a draft runbook (fastpatch_runbook_v1.pdf) and a short KV-drain checklist. Please reply with: readiness (yes/no), any gating items, and your preferred window.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: fastpatch_runbook_v1.pdf (doc), kv_drain_checklist.txt (text)
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private fastpatch readiness & escape plan for AcmeHealth VPC

Tessa,

Readiness: yes, with the following notes from infra/SRE side.
- KV cache drain: our current drain script is safe for in-flight sessions but has a ~45s median drain per node on 2M-key sets. I attached kv_drain_checklist.txt with a timing table.
- Pinning: recommend using temporary version-tag pin (agent.pinned_version) rather than full deployment lock to avoid scheduler churn. Pin/unpin calls are in the runbook (section 2).
- Canary: I support 5% -> 20% ramp, but we should target a 3-node canary (single AZ) first to avoid cross-AZ network flaps.

Automation snippets I will push to the runbook before Friday:
- drain_and_pin.sh (stub)
- telemetry assertions (P95 latency, error spike detection)

Ops@Acme: please confirm whether your secondary region (us-east-1) prefers Saturday window.

Dev
Principal SRE, Redwood

Thanks — a couple of operational concerns to call out: 
1) Network drain time variance: For nodes behind our larger inference pods, TCP TIME_WAIT can cause drain tails up to 4 minutes in bad cases. If we stack many nodes in a canary we may see transient error spikes that aren't caused by the patch. Consider staggering the canary by AZ with 5m gaps.
2) Service pinning implications: Pinning the control agent is fine, but ensure the autoscaler control-plane has a soft cap so we don't cause an autoscale storm during drains. Add a pre-step: set autoscaler.max_surge=0 for the cohort.
3) Rollback plan: I prefer a two-stage rollback: (a) unpin + revert control agent, (b) if still bad, promote standby images and force restart only for affected AZ. This reduces blast radius.

I've copied a short canary_matrix.csv in attachments that maps node counts to expected drain times.

Karthik
VP, Infrastructure

Thanks everyone — decision and next steps below.

Decision: Option B (Sat 2028-07-06 02:00-05:00 PT). Rationale: gives ops buffer and more time for prep, minimizes US weekday risk.

Canary plan (final):
- Step 0: Pre-step (Fri 2028-07-05 22:00 PT) set autoscaler.max_surge=0 for target cohort.
- Step 1: Canary (3 nodes, single AZ) 02:00 PT -> 02:15 PT (monitor 15m)
- Step 2: Ramp to 20% across AZs 02:20 PT -> 02:45 PT (monitor 25m)
- Step 3: Full fleet (remainder) 02:50 PT -> 04:30 PT (staggered by AZ)

Rollback triggers (stringent):
- P95 increase > 40% lasting > 5m
- Error rate spike > 0.5% lasting > 5m
- Any persistent healthcheck fail on > 2 nodes in 1 AZ

Rollback procedure (summary):
1) Unpin control agent (automated via drain_and_pin.sh --rollback)
2) If metrics do not recover in 10m, force promote standby image + AZ restart for affected nodes
3) Post-incident: create incident report, schedule follow-up with Acme, attach telemetry graphs

Pre-reqs before Fri 22:00 PT:
- Dev: push drain_and_pin.sh and telemetry assertions into runbook (Dev)
- Jasmine: confirm dashboard alerts and add Sat on-call alias to the dashboard
- Karthik: ensure autoscaler soft cap toggle is tested in staging
- Marissa: procurement: confirm we have spare CI capacity and confirm tier-2 on-call compensation approval for the Sat window

Ops@Acme: please confirm a backup contact and whether Saturday 02:00 PT is acceptable. Once Acme confirms, we'll post a scheduled maintenance notice and a calendar invite.

Thanks — green light pending external confirmation.

Tessa Morgan
Sr. PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
